reference_customer_basis: Conditional components are left out of modeled costs unless an entry below says that the reference (typical) customer of the sector pays them (user decision, October 9, 2026). An entry applies to components of its province and fuel, for the listed sectors (residential or a commercial size band), whose notes (after the 'Provenance: ...' prefix) fully match notes_regex and whose component name fully matches name_regex (Python re.fullmatch; every given pattern must match). Only components otherwise excluded as 'conditional' qualify: alternatives, optional components, expired or not-yet-effective components and value-less market components stay excluded. Included components are itemized with reason 'reference_customer:<id>'. Ontario reference customers: residential and GS < 50 kW customers are on the Regulated Price Plan (RPP) and buy from their distributor (standard supply); customers at the 50 kW and over levels buy spot-priced energy through their distributor (non-RPP standard supply); all are Class B (not Industrial Conservation Initiative participants) and none is a wholesale market participant. Still excluded: the Hydro One RRRP credit (principal-residence condition), EV charging rates, former Chapleau PUC rider sets, transformer-ownership allowances, primary-metering and transformer-loss allowances, and meter-type, interval-meter and demand-size alternatives.

match.notes_regex: ^Conditional: Applies only to Class B customers(?:; (?:In effect until the effective date of the next cost-of-service rate order|Approved on an interim basis|Published per 30 days))*$

Every reference customer is Class B: RPP residential and GS < 50 kW customers, and 50 kW and over customers that do not take part in the Industrial Conservation Initiative (Class A).

fixed_charge_variants_basis: A fixed charge published as variants of one charge by phase or service size (amperage), either as unconditional variants such as 'Basic Customer Charge (Single Phase)' / 'Basic Customer Charge (Three Phase)' or as alternatives marked 'Alternative: applies only to ...', is priced for the reference customer of the usage level (user decision, October 30, 2026): homes are single-phase service of 200 A; small businesses (commercial under 50 kW) are single-phase at the 10 kW level (s1) and three-phase at the 25 kW level (s2). For each such group, the rule of the model's fuel, sector and level selects the variant whose component name fully matches match.name_regex (Python re.fullmatch). Exactly one matching variant with a value per month is priced and itemized with reason 'fixed_charge_variant:<id>'; no match or more than one leaves the record not computable at that level with the existing reason. Other sectors and levels have no rule, so their variants stay not computable.

fixed_charge_variants.note: Selects the variant whose range covers a 200 A single-phase home. Live variants on 2026-10-30: Newfoundland Power 1.1 and NL Hydro 1.1 'Basic Customer Charge (Not Exceeding 200 Amp Service)' (not '(Exceeding 200 Amp Service)').

basis: Monthly usage levels approved by the user on October 9, 2026: residential 500/1,000/2,000 kWh; commercial under 50 kW at 2,000 kWh with 10 kW and 8,000 kWh with 25 kW; 50-499 kW at 40,000 kWh with 100 kW; 500-4,999 kW at 500,000 kWh with 1,000 kW; no level yet for 5,000 kW and over. Daily charges convert to monthly at 30.4375 days (365.25 / 12); hours per month 730.5. kVA demand is derived from kW at the disclosed 0.9 power factor (kVA = kW / 0.9) and never treated as kW. Implied load factors (kWh / (kW x 730.5)): s1 27.4%, s2 43.8%, m1 54.8%, l1 68.4%. Levels are comparison points for modeled costs, not a load profile of any customer.
